text: Joseph came and told Pharaoh, "My father and my brothers have come from the land of Canaan with their flocks and herds and everything they own, and they are now in the land of Goshen."

versions.text: Joseph went and told Pharaoh, "My father and my brothers have come from the land of Canaan with their flocks and herds and everything they own, and they are now in the land of Goshen."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb is בּוֹא ("came"), matching the same verb used of the family's arrival later in the verse. "Came" preserves the repetition and the perspective of the narrative (Joseph coming into Pharaoh's presence).

text: He had taken five of his brothers with him, and he presented them to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh asked his brothers, "What is your occupation?" They answered Pharaoh, "Your servants are shepherds, as our fathers were before us."

They said to Pharaoh, "We have come to live in this land for a while, because there is no pasture for your servants' flocks; the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Please, let your servants settle in the land of Goshen."
Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Your father and your brothers have come to you.

The land of Egypt lies open before you. Settle your father and your brothers in the best part of the land; let them live in the land of Goshen. And if you know of capable men among them, put them in charge of my own livestock."
Then Joseph brought in his father Jacob and presented him to Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Pharaoh asked Jacob, "How many are the years of your life?"

Jacob answered Pharaoh, "The years of my sojourning are a hundred and thirty. Few and hard have been the years of my life, and they do not measure up to the years of my fathers during their sojourning."
Then Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from his presence.
So Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them property in the best part of the land of Egypt, in the district of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
And Joseph provided his father, his brothers, and all his father's household with food, according to the number of their children.
There was no food anywhere in the land, for the famine was severe. Egypt and Canaan alike wasted away because of it.
Joseph collected all the money to be found in Egypt and Canaan in payment for the grain the people were buying, and he brought it into Pharaoh's palace.
When the money of Egypt and Canaan was gone, all the Egyptians came to Joseph and said, "Give us food! Why should we die before your eyes? Our money is spent."
Joseph said, "Bring your livestock, and I will give you food in exchange for it, since your money is gone."

versions.text: Joseph said, "Bring your livestock, and I will sell you food in exchange for it, since your money is gone."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb is נָתַן ("give"), and "sell ... in exchange for" is both a doublet and a shift in nuance. "Give ... in exchange for" is accurate and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and he gave them food in exchange for their horses, their flocks and herds, and their donkeys. That year he carried them through with food in exchange for all their livestock.

When that year had ended, they came to him the next year and said, "We cannot hide it from my lord: our money is gone, and our herds belong to my lord. Nothing is left for my lord but our bodies and our land.

Why should we perish before your eyes, we and our land as well? Buy us and our land in exchange for food, and we with our land will be servants to Pharaoh. Give us seed, so that we may live and not die, and the land may not become desolate."
So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh. Every Egyptian sold his field, because the famine pressed hard upon them, and the land became Pharaoh's.
As for the people, he moved them into the cities, from one end of Egypt to the other.
Only the land of the priests he did not buy, for the priests had a fixed allowance from Pharaoh and lived on the allowance Pharaoh gave them; that is why they did not sell their land.
Then Joseph said to the people, "Now that I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh, here is seed for you. Sow the land.
At harvest time you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh. The other four fifths will be yours as seed for the fields and as food for yourselves, your households, and your children."
They said, "You have saved our lives. May we find favor in the eyes of my lord; we will be servants to Pharaoh."
So Joseph made it a statute concerning the land of Egypt, still in force today, that a fifth belongs to Pharaoh. Only the land of the priests did not become Pharaoh's.
Israel settled in Egypt, in the land of Goshen. They acquired property there, and they were fruitful and increased greatly in number.
Jacob lived seventeen years in the land of Egypt, so that the years of his life came to a hundred and forty-seven.

When the time drew near for Israel to die, he called for his son Joseph and said to him, "If I have found favor in your eyes, put your hand under my thigh and deal with me in kindness and faithfulness: do not bury me in Egypt.

versions.text: When the time drew near for Israel to die, he called for his son Joseph and said to him, "If I have found favor in your eyes, put your hand under my thigh and promise to show me kindness and faithfulness: do not bury me in Egypt.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says "do with me kindness and faithfulness"; "promise" introduces an idea not in the text (the oath is requested separately in v. 31).

text: When I rest with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me where they are buried." Joseph said, "I will do as you say."
"Swear it to me," he said. So Joseph swore to him, and Israel bowed down at the head of his bed.

versions.text: "Swear it to me," he said. So Joseph swore to him, and Israel bowed in worship at the head of his bed.
versions.explanation: The rendering is defensible, but "in worship" is an interpretive addition; the verb simply means to bow low. A footnote could note that an ancient Greek reading understood the unpointed Hebrew as "leaning on the top of his staff."
